commits.message:
fix(style): every default style that paints a ground is readable on every bundled theme (rich-syntax-60ii)

Review of #271: the per-Syntax contrast test checked one style on two themes.
The sweep now lives on DEFAULT_STYLES, where the invariant is, and it caught
markdown.code (cyan on grey11, 3.57:1 on the default theme) -> dark_turquoise.
16-colour depth is filed as rich-contrast-sqqq.

fix(syntax): a highlighted line number is readable on a light terminal (rich-syntax-60ii)

syntax.line_number.highlight set a fixed grey27 ground but took its ink
from the terminal theme, so on a light theme the numbers were dark on dark
grey (contrast 1.16 under ATOM_ONE_LIGHT). The ink is now grey93, from the
same fixed palette, and a test holds both example themes to WCAG 4.5.

fix(live): printing through live.console lands above the frame (rich-live-sadk) (#270)

* fix(live): printing through live.console lands above the frame (rich-live-sadk)

A Console now holds at most one LiveRegion, and every write it makes steps
around it: the frame is erased, the write lands where it was, and the frame
is painted again underneath — Rich's render-hook model. Live claims the
region from start() to the hand-back; claiming a second on the same console
throws instead of corrupting both displays.

* fix(live): a print through live.console reaches the terminal in one write, and keeps a line it stops mid-way (rich-live-sadk)

LiveRegion.around is now text in, bytes out: the console writes the erase,
the text and the repainted frame as one chunk. Painter.around ends text that
stops mid-line before the frame repaints over it. A stale claimLiveRegion
release leaves a newer claim in place. docs/live.md's warning named the
wrong console.
